punchline: Duhigg offered practical fixes to people who wanted empathy, and wanted outrage from a wife who offered fixes.
thirty_sec: Charles Duhigg, with a Harvard MBA, struggled as a manager at The New York Times: colleagues felt unheard because he offered fixes when they wanted empathy. At home the pattern ran the other way, with his wife suggesting a lunch with his boss when he wanted her outrage.
question: Who in your life do you usually answer with a solution, and what might they actually be hoping you will give them?
key_contrast: Each of them tried to help in a conversation the other was not having.
